entries.title: I Kings 17:1
segments:
According to my word; as he should foretell and pray for it. 
 
Instead of at once destroying the wicked as they deserve, God often waits long upon them, visits them with judgments and with mercies, and does all that infinite wisdom and goodness can consistently do to lead them to repent, and thus to escape the destruction which continued wickedness and impenitence will bring upon them.

entries.title: I Kings 17:6
segments: Neither the fowls of the air nor the beasts of the field ever rebel against the will of their Creator, nor do they refuse to do what he bids them.

entries.title: I Kings 17:9
segments: Zarephath; a city on the Mediterranean, between Tyre and Zidon; in the New Testament, Sarepta.
When one means of supply fails those who trust in God, he will provide for them another, and in obeying him they never will want any thing necessary to their highest good.

entries.title: I Kings 17:11
segments: God often requires of his people what nothing but strong faith and active benevolence will lead them to do.

entries.title: I Kings 17:15
segments: Confidence in the promises of God, manifested by acting under a conviction of their truth, will not be disappointed, but will be followed by timely and abundant supplies.

entries.title: I Kings 17:17
segments: No exercise of faith in God, love to his friends, or readiness to honor him in doing them good, will secure us from liability to great and sore trials.  It is only through much tribulation that any are prepared to enter the kingdom of God.

entries.title: I Kings 17:18
segments:
Slay my son; she supposed her afflictions might have been as a punishment for her sins, and brought upon her by God through the instrumentality of the prophet. 
 
All our sufferings are caused by our sins, and should lead us more and more to loathe and forsake them, trusting in Christ for pardon, and for all which we need to do the will of God, and meet his gracious acceptance.

entries.title: I Kings 17:24
segments:
In thy mouth is truth; she knew that what the prophet had declared was true, and would be accomplished. 
 
To those who obey God, he so manifests himself as to convince them that all his declarations will be surely and fully accomplished.
